content.user_title: Convert Line Drawings to Verified SVG Paths
content.value_statement: Raster diagrams are difficult to edit and compare after tracing. This workflow creates SVG paths, optionally recovers selected regions, and produces rendered previews with comparison evidence.
actual_capabilities: Trace dark line art into grayscale SVG paths while preserving normalized canvas dimensions.
Remove suitable bright flat fills with the optional channel-max signal while retaining neutral ink.
Recover named closed regions from explicit seed points, barrier repairs, clipping polygons, and exclusions.
Generate a PNG render, normalized reference, ink overlay, difference image, and comparison report.
Check generated SVG for embedded images, executable content, external asset references, duplicate IDs, and unclosed editable subpaths.
Report ink F1, foreground RMSE, boundary distance, region overlap, and source and output checksums.
limitations: Requires Python 3.10+, Potrace, and the Python dependencies; the helper does not install them.
Targets dark line art on bright backgrounds, not photographs or faithful full-color conversion.
Input transparency is composited on white; channel-max can erase colored strokes and retain dark fills.
Region identity and reconstructed borders require human review; visual metrics do not establish semantic correctness or pixel-perfect equivalence.

use_cases.title: Prepare Editable Diagram Assets
use_cases.description: Convert scanned line diagrams into SVG paths and review rendered differences before importing them into a design workflow.

use_cases.title: Recover Named Illustration Regions
use_cases.description: Select diagram compartments with seed points and documented barrier repairs to create separately editable closed paths.

use_cases.title: Check Converted Documentation Figures
use_cases.description: Generate previews, overlays, and structural evidence for line-art figures intended for technical documentation.

prompt_templates.title: Trace a Line Drawing
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert [input image] into SVG paths using luminance and a new output directory. Provide the SVG, PNG preview, and verification summary.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: convert dark line art on a white background.

prompt_templates.title: Remove Suitable Bright Fills
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect [input image] for channel-max suitability. Remove bright flat fills while preserving neutral ink, and disclose any colored strokes that could disappear.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: remove explicitly unwanted bright fills.

prompt_templates.title: Recover Editable Regions
prompt_templates.prompt: Trace [input image] and recover [requested regions] using source-coordinate seeds. Record necessary repairs, preserve meaningful holes, and review region boundaries separately from ink.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: produce named closed regions for editing.

prompt_templates.title: Refine and Verify a Trace
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [input image], [region specification], and [existing report]. Refine relevant trace or region settings, write a new output directory, and summarize comparisons and uncertainties.
prompt_templates.scenario: Expert: iterate on tracing and region recovery without replacing existing artifacts.

output_examples.input: A dark line diagram on a white background, with no requested region recovery.
output: SVG paths at the normalized source dimensions, with no embedded source bitmap.
PNG preview, normalized reference, ink overlay, and absolute difference image.
Report containing structural checks, comparison metrics, and source and SVG checksums.

output_examples.input: A two-compartment diagram with explicit seeds and a documented repair across a border gap.
output: Separate named closed paths beneath the visible ink layer.
Region recovery details including overlap pixels, clipping status, and barrier repair count.
Verification summary identifying the reconstructed border and the need for visual review.

best_practices: Inspect the source before selecting luminance or explicitly requested channel-max preprocessing.
Keep region specifications in source-pixel coordinates and document all reconstructed borders.
Review overlays and boundaries at original scale alongside metrics, and use a new output directory for each iteration.
anti_patterns: Apply channel-max automatically to colored handwriting, photographs, or assets requiring faithful color.
Treat ink similarity scores or path counts as proof of correct region identity.
Optimize file size before checking fine details, named regions, and comparison images.

faq.question: Does the SVG contain the original bitmap?
faq.answer: No. The helper generates SVG paths and checks for embedded image elements.

faq.question: Can it preserve photographs or every original color?
faq.answer: No. It targets neutral line art and uses a limited grayscale palette, not faithful photographic or full-color reconstruction.

faq.question: Does it discover semantic objects automatically?
faq.answer: No. Editable regions require explicit seed selections and optional repairs or clips. Region names and inferred boundaries need visual review.

faq.question: What does verification compare?
faq.answer: It compares a rendered SVG with the normalized target using ink overlap, grayscale error, and boundary distance. Structural checks are separate.

faq.question: Does tracing upload the image or install software?
faq.answer: The helper processes local files without a hosted API and does not install dependencies. Python packages and Potrace must already be available.

faq.question: Will it change my input or replace existing outputs?
faq.answer: The helper guards against overwriting the input and refuses existing output files unless --overwrite is supplied. Use a separate output directory.
